messages.author: c796dce9bb2d010b
messages.subject: ‘uniform_cdf’ was not declared in this scope
parts:
Hi,

and first of all, thank you to the whole team who created (R)Stan, this is most valuable!

I tried to fit a simple linear hierarchical model (but with no intercept). The model is as follow : 

data {
int<lower=0> J; 
int<lower=0> n; 
int<lower=1,upper=J> dpt[n]; 
real<lower=0,upper=100> x1[n]; 
real<lower=0,upper=100> y[n];
}
transformed data {
real<lower=0,upper=100> x2[n];
x2[n] <- 100 - x1[n];
}
parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> beta1[J];
real<lower=0,upper=1> beta2[J];
real<lower=0,upper=1> beta1_mu; 
real<lower=0,upper=1> beta2_mu;
real<lower=0> sigma_y; // variance de y
real<lower=0> sigma_beta1; // variances des coefficients
real<lower=0> sigma_beta2;
}
model {

// priors

beta1_mu ~ normal(0, 1) T[0,1]; 
beta2_mu ~ normal(0, 1) T[0,1];
sigma_beta1 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];
sigma_beta2 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];
beta1 ~ normal(beta1_mu, sigma_beta1) T[0,1];
beta2 ~ normal(beta2_mu, sigma_beta2) T[0,1];

sigma_y ~ uniform(0, 1000);

// Likelihood
for (i in 1:n) {

y[i] ~ normal(beta1[dpt[i]] * x1[i] + beta2[dpt[i]] * x2[i], sigma_y);

}
}



When I try to run it, the compilation encounters an error. The complete output is attached, but the relevant part seems to be "‘uniform_cdf’ was not declared in this scope". Any idea as to where my mistake might be?
(For the record, when I tried to run examples from the mc-stan.org site, it worked, so my configuration should be OK. I run R 2.15.1 on Ubuntu 11.10). 

Thank you very much,

Joel

We are in the process of implementing the cumulative distribution
functions for all the densities, so support for truncated
distributions is limited as of v1.0.1.

With regards to your model, you do not need to truncate the uniform
distribution since the parameters sigma_beta1 and sigma_beta2 are
already bounded in their declaration. All you need to do to have your
model be compilable is to replace
<code>

sigma_beta1 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];
sigma_beta2 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];

</code>

with:
<code>
sigma_beta1 ~ uniform(0, 1000);
sigma_beta2 ~ uniform(0, 1000);
</code>

You could also remove the truncation statements for beta1_mu,
beta2_mu, beta1, and beta2. The models should behave identically with
and without the truncation statements.

Please let us know if that fixes the issue with your model.



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ‘uniform_cdf’ was not declared in this scope
parts:
Two more issues.

One, you want to run to convergence, say all R-hat values
under 1.1 or so.

Second, you need to constrain parameters to match their
support in the model:

>> parameters {
...

>> real<lower=0> sigma_beta1; // variances des coefficients
>> real<lower=0> sigma_beta2;

...
>> model {
...

>> sigma_beta1 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];
>> sigma_beta2 ~ uniform(0, 1000) T[0,];

sigma_beta1 and sigma_beta2 should be declared
as real<lower=0,upper=1000>. At this point, the
uniform distribution is implicit, but adding
it to the model won't hurt (Stan's smart enough
not to do the redundant calculations).

You should eliminate these truncation statements,
though, as they're redundant. Restriction of
variables to a range happens in their declarations
in the parameters block. Truncation just changes
the distribution.

- Bob

parts:
